stem: In the context of the coagulation cascade, why is Factor $XIII$ deficiency NOT picked up by routine PT or APTT screening tests?

options.text: Factor $XIII$ is only found in the platelets, not the plasma.
It functions to cross-link fibrin after the initial clot is formed, which occurs after the endpoint of those tests.
Factor $XIII$ is part of the extrinsic pathway, which only the INR measures.
It is an inhibitor rather than a factor.

explanation: PT and APTT measure the time to the initial formation of fibrin; Factor $XIII$ works subsequently to stabilize the clot, so its absence doesn't delay the initial 'mesh' formation.
rationale: Think about the very last step in the 'dreaded' cascade diagram.

optionExplanations.A: Factor $XIII$ is a plasma protein, but its specific role is at the end of the clotting process.
optionExplanations.B: PT and APTT measure the time to the initial formation of fibrin; Factor $XIII$ works subsequently to stabilize the clot, so its absence doesn't delay the initial 'mesh' formation.
optionExplanations.C: The INR is just a calculation of the PT; neither measures Factor $XIII$.
optionExplanations.D: Factor $XIII$ is a pro-coagulant factor, though its deficiency leads to unstable clots.
